common.comment: Checkpoint from https://sites.ecmwf.int/repository/fiab/ecmwf/checkpoints/demo/aifs-global-v1.ckpt (the former testing/checkpoints/aifs-global-o48.ckpt). torch is pinned to 2.8.0 instead of 2.6.0: torch 2.6 has no CUDA build with kernels for the GB10 (sm_121), so it ran on the CPU; 2.8.0+cu129 has sm_120 kernels, which run on it.

Checkpoint from https://sites.ecmwf.int/repository/fiab/metno/checkpoints/demo/bris-europe-v1.ckpt, which is testing/checkpoints/bris-europe-0.5-o48-20251017.ckpt with the grid_indices supporting array removed: it is a (20657, 1) array of ones, which anemoi-inference>=0.13 uses to index the model latitudes/longitudes, collapsing every grid point onto the second one. anemoi-graphs is bumped from 0.6.6 to 0.8.3, the first release allowing numpy 2: 0.6.6 downgrades the worker to numpy 1.26, which cannot read task outputs written with numpy 2.

Checkpoint from https://sites.ecmwf.int/repository/fiab/fmi/checkpoints/aila/aila-nordic-v2.0.ckpt (the former fmi/checkpoints/aila-2.0.ckpt). Uses locally patched anemoi-plugins-ecmwf wheels (built from main 48df67a): the regrid to 'checkpoint:source0' coordinates is silently skipped by the released 0.7.0/0.2.0 plugins, as normalise_grid turns the coordinate dict into a string MIR ignores, and RegridPreprocessor reads coordinates from the unstructured_grid GRIB output, which has none. MIR is pinned to 1.28.1.19: mir-python 1.30.2.33 segfaults regridding to unstructured grids above a few hundred points. ANEMOI_INFERENCE_NUM_CHUNKS is raised from 16 to 64 to reduce the inference memory peak. Uses a locally patched earthkit-workflows-anemoi wheel (0.9.0+fiab4, which also has the Varda fixes): CascadeRunner builds its RunConfiguration directly instead of through RunConfiguration.load, so the configuration env (control_options) is never applied; the patch also lets runner_options set output_templates. The output uses a GRIB template on the MEPS Lambert grid (949x1069, 2.5 km, LaD/Latin 63.3, LoV 15, sphere of 6371000 m), so the LAM output is lambert GRIB rather than unstructured_grid. The LAM input is fetched on a 0.1/0.1 grid, the native grid of the high-resolution open data, cropped to 77/-20/48/56 (the Lambert domain plus at least a 1 degree margin), and then regridded to the checkpoint coordinates.

Checkpoint from https://sites.ecmwf.int/repository/fiab/metno/checkpoints/bris/bris-nordic-v2025.10.ckpt (the former metnorway/checkpoints/bris-2025_10.ckpt). Changes from the shared entry: the LAM region is lam_0 (the checkpoint masks are lam_0/cutout_mask and global/cutout_mask); the anemoi-graphs==0.6.6 pin, which forces numpy<2, is dropped as the pickled model does not import anemoi.graphs; locally patched anemoi-plugins-ecmwf wheels make the regrid to 'checkpoint:source0' coordinates work, with MIR pinned to 1.28.1.19; a locally patched earthkit-workflows-anemoi applies control_options and allows output_templates; the output uses a GRIB template on the trimmed MEPS Lambert grid (849x969, 2.5 km, LaD/Latin 63.3, LoV 15, sphere of 6371000 m). The LAM input is fetched on a 0.1/0.1 grid, the native grid of the high-resolution open data, cropped to 76/-15/49/51 (the Lambert domain plus at least a 1 degree margin), and then regridded to the checkpoint coordinates.

Checkpoint from https://sites.ecmwf.int/repository/fiab/metno/checkpoints/demo/bris-africa-v1.0.ckpt (the former metnorway/checkpoints/graceful-gazelle.ckpt). MIR is pinned to 1.28.1.19, with anemoi-plugins-ecmwf-inference 0.7.0 and anemoi-plugins-ecmwf-transform 0.2.0: with mir-python 1.30.2.33 the O1280 area crop of the LAM input gives fields whose values (1,011,620) do not match their GRIB geometry (1,211,892 points), which fails in the orog_to_z pre-processor of anemoi-plugins-ecmwf-inference 0.8.0; anemoi-plugins-ecmwf-transform 0.3.0 builds the mir output templates with a MIR grid spec that MIR 1.28 rejects, so the output falls back to arrays without a grid.

Nested BRIS model over New Zealand: a 2.5 km Lambert conformal LAM (849x969, LaD -41, LoV 172.5, sphere R=6371229 m, fitted to the checkpoint coordinates) inside a global N320 grid, trained on IFS analyses. Uses the same patched wheels as BRIS-2025.10 and a local Lambert GRIB template. Both inputs set their grid and area explicitly, as the metadata lookup finds the LAM data request first, whose grid is null and whose area is only partly set; the global input uses the N320 grid and a null area (no crop). The LAM input is fetched on a 0.1/0.1 grid, the native grid of the high-resolution open data, cropped to -28/156/-53/189 (the Lambert domain plus at least a 1 degree margin), and then regridded to the checkpoint coordinates.

Nested anemoi model over Italy and the Alps from ECMWF (G. Balsamo), for internal evaluation only: a 3 arcmin LAM (regular 0.05 deg grid at the cell centres, 120 x 260 points, 48.975/4.025/43.025/16.975) inside a global O160 grid, trained on ERA5 and CERRA 2017-2025, with a 2->12 step rollout fine-tune (the recommended one of the two checkpoints in checkpoint/italy). Uses released packages only. The LAM input is fetched directly on the checkpoint grid (0.05/0.05 with the exact area: MIR produces the grid shifted by half a cell), so no regrid to the checkpoint coordinates and no output template are needed; the global input uses O160 and a null area. mir-python is pinned to 1.28.1.19: with 1.30 (eccodes 2.50) and the ECCODES_ECKIT_GEO=1 that anemoi-plugins-ecmwf-transform 0.3.0 sets, regular_ll still works but this combination was not tested.
